rows.label: Edgar Allan Poe
rows.hook: wrote "The Raven" and macabre tales like "The Tell-Tale Heart"

rows.label: Sylvia Plath
rows.hook: wrote the semi-autobiographical novel "The Bell Jar" and the poetry collection "Ariel"

rows.label: Dante Alighieri
rows.hook: wrote "The Divine Comedy," a journey through Hell, Purgatory and Paradise

rows.label: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
rows.description: German writer, artist, natural scientist and politician (1749–1832)
rows.hook: wrote the drama "Faust," about a scholar who bargains with the devil

rows.label: Rabindranath Tagore
rows.hook: became the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature

rows.label: Victor Hugo
rows.description: French novelist, poet, dramatist and politician (1802–1885)
rows.hook: wrote "Les Misérables" and "The Hunchback of Notre-Dame"

rows.label: Emily Brontë
rows.hook: wrote the only novel "Wuthering Heights," set on the windswept moors

rows.label: Lewis Carroll
rows.hook: wrote "Alice's Adventures in Wonderland" and the nonsense poem "Jabberwocky"

rows.label: Walt Whitman
rows.hook: wrote the free-verse collection "Leaves of Grass" and "O Captain! My Captain!"

rows.label: Allen Ginsberg
rows.hook: wrote the Beat Generation poem "Howl," which faced an obscenity trial

rows.label: Emily Dickinson
rows.hook: was a reclusive poet of short, dash-filled poems who published almost nothing in life

rows.label: Alexander Pushkin
rows.hook: wrote the verse novel "Eugene Onegin" and is called the founder of modern literature in his homeland

rows.label: Jorge Luis Borges
rows.description: Argentine writer, essayist, poet and translator (1899–1986)
rows.hook: wrote labyrinthine short stories like "The Library of Babel" and "The Aleph"

rows.label: Ralph Waldo Emerson
rows.hook: was a leading Transcendentalist who wrote the essay "Self-Reliance"

rows.label: Virgil
rows.hook: wrote the "Aeneid," the epic of a Trojan hero who founds a great empire's line

rows.label: Federico García Lorca
rows.description: Spanish poet, dramatist and prose writer (1898–1936)
rows.hook: wrote "Blood Wedding" and "Gypsy Ballads" before being killed at the start of a civil war

rows.label: Geoffrey Chaucer
rows.hook: wrote "The Canterbury Tales," stories told by pilgrims on the road to a shrine

rows.label: Ovid
rows.hook: wrote the "Metamorphoses," a long poem of myths in which people change shape

rows.label: William Butler Yeats
rows.hook: wrote "The Second Coming" and "The Lake Isle of Innisfree" and won a Nobel Prize

rows.label: John Milton
rows.hook: wrote "Paradise Lost," an epic about Satan's fall and Adam and Eve

rows.label: Thomas Hardy
rows.hook: wrote "Tess of the d'Urbervilles" and "Far from the Madding Crowd" before turning mainly to verse

rows.label: Robert Frost
rows.hook: wrote "The Road Not Taken" and "Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening"

rows.label: Christopher Marlowe
rows.hook: wrote "Doctor Faustus" and "Tamburlaine" and was a rival of Shakespeare

rows.label: John Keats
rows.hook: wrote "Ode to a Nightingale" and "Ode on a Grecian Urn" and died very young

rows.label: Sappho
rows.description: ancient Greek poet from Lesbos (c. 630-c. 570 BC)
rows.hook: was an ancient poet of love lyrics whose work survives mostly in fragments

rows.label: Langston Hughes
rows.hook: was a leading voice of the Harlem Renaissance who wrote "The Negro Speaks of Rivers"

rows.label: Samuel Johnson
rows.hook: compiled "A Dictionary of the English Language" almost single-handedly

rows.label: Henrik Ibsen
rows.hook: wrote the plays "A Doll's House" and "Peer Gynt"

rows.label: Jonathan Swift
rows.hook: wrote "Gulliver's Travels" and the satire "A Modest Proposal"

rows.label: Pablo Neruda
rows.hook: wrote "Twenty Love Poems and a Song of Despair" and won a Nobel Prize

rows.label: Charles Baudelaire
rows.hook: wrote the controversial collection "Les Fleurs du mal" (The Flowers of Evil)

rows.label: Arthur Rimbaud
rows.hook: was a teenage prodigy who wrote "The Drunken Boat" and quit poetry by age twenty-one

rows.label: Anne Brontë
rows.hook: wrote the novel "The Tenant of Wildfell Hall" and was the youngest of three famous literary sisters

rows.label: Robert Burns
rows.hook: wrote "Auld Lang Syne" and "To a Mouse" and is celebrated each year with a supper

rows.label: Alfred Tennyson
rows.hook: wrote "The Charge of the Light Brigade" and "Ulysses" and served as Poet Laureate for decades

rows.label: Petrarch
rows.hook: popularized a fourteen-line love-poem form named after him, written for a woman called Laura

rows.label: Martial
rows.hook: was a Latin master of the short, witty, pointed poem called the epigram

rows.label: Muhammad Iqbal
rows.description: British-Indian Islamic philosopher, poet and politician (1877-1938)
rows.hook: wrote poetry in Urdu and Persian and is honored as the national poet of Pakistan

rows.label: Hesiod
rows.description: ancient Greek poet of the archaic period
rows.hook: wrote "Theogony" and "Works and Days" about the origins of the gods and farm life

rows.label: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
rows.hook: wrote "The Song of Hiawatha" and "Paul Revere's Ride"

rows.label: Elizabeth Barrett Browning
rows.hook: wrote "Sonnets from the Portuguese," including "How do I love thee? Let me count the ways"

rows.label: Horace
rows.hook: wrote the Odes and coined the phrase "carpe diem" (seize the day)

rows.label: John Donne
rows.hook: wrote "No man is an island" and was a leading Metaphysical poet who became a dean of St Paul's

rows.label: Seamus Heaney
rows.hook: won the Nobel Prize in Literature and wrote "Digging" and "Death of a Naturalist"

rows.label: Jean Racine
rows.hook: wrote the tragedies "Phèdre" and "Andromaque" in rhymed twelve-syllable verse

rows.label: Omar Khayyám
rows.hook: is known for the "Rubaiyat," quatrains about wine and fleeting life, and also for mathematics

rows.label: Ben Jonson
rows.hook: wrote the comedy "Volpone" and was a friend and rival of Shakespeare

rows.label: John of the Cross
rows.description: Spanish mystic and Roman Catholic saint (1542–1591)
rows.hook: wrote "Dark Night of the Soul," a mystic poem about the soul's journey toward God

rows.label: Wole Soyinka
rows.hook: became the first African to win the Nobel Prize in Literature

rows.label: Paul Verlaine
rows.hook: was a Symbolist poet who wrote "Autumn Song" and had a stormy relationship with a teenage fellow poet

rows.label: Catullus
rows.description: lyric Latin poet of the Roman Republic
rows.hook: wrote passionate love poems to a woman he called Lesbia

rows.label: Carl Sandburg
rows.hook: wrote "Chicago" ("City of the Big Shoulders") and a Pulitzer-winning biography of Lincoln

rows.label: Li Bai
rows.description: Classical Chinese poet of the Tang dynasty (701–762)
rows.hook: is famed for verses about wine, the moon and wandering, and is called a poet-immortal
